file_decisions.evidence: AnalyticsConsent and AnalyticsRouteTracker are already mounted. The dirty Neemuch routes depend on untracked page/data files and are outside the consent change.
The Analytics Preferences control is already present. The current Delivery Requests link is retained.

Both analytics identifiers and the updated policy date are present. The current branch also validates the GA identifier and provides the synchronized public fallback instead of silently disabling analytics.

The current add_to_cart event carries product, variant, price, and quantity fields directly. Replacing it with the dirty wrapper would add an untracked dependency and regress the current atomic multi-variant inventory check.

The dirty homepage change is an SEO/navigation surface requiring untracked Neemuch data and page dependencies, not an analytics-consent implementation. The current synchronized merchandising and promo components are retained.
The consent-gated Google Analytics and Meta Pixel disclosure, withdrawal path, prohibited data list, and query/fragment exclusion are already present.

The current implementation retains consent storage, delayed tracker loading, revocation, cookie expiry, and sensitive-route suppression while using the real arguments object required by Google Consent Mode. Dirty query/referrer forwarding is rejected because the published notice says query strings and fragments are excluded.

privacy_invariants: Google Analytics and Meta Pixel remain off until explicit acceptance.
Declining or withdrawing consent revokes tracker consent and expires known analytics cookies.
Order-success, order-tracking, and reset-password routes are not tracked.
Page locations exclude query strings and fragments.
The active Google Consent Mode shim queues the standard arguments object.
production_claim: No tracker, environment, consent value, deployment, service, or production state was changed.
